route_under_evaluation.$comment: Reconstructed from docs/data/apparatus-search-broadened-v1.json. Mission 1.58 described the two apparatuses without naming them, which was right for a class survey. Mission 1.59 has to read their actual documentation and hand a named pair to a governance mission, so they are named here. The requirements record stays source-free, as Mission 1.48 established.
route_under_evaluation.why_not_substituted: Section 1. Mission 1.59 evaluates the route Mission 1.58 found. Swapping in a pair that is easier to document would be answering a different question and calling it closure.

apparatus_a.interface: the Censys Platform host dataset and its search API
apparatus_a.claimed_construct: hosts and the services observed on them across the public IPv4 space
apparatus_a.scan_model: its own scanners attempt a small number of connections to every IPv4 address, then complete protocol handshakes

apparatus_b.interface: the Netlas responses collection and its search API
apparatus_b.claimed_construct: service responses captured while sweeping the IPv4 space against a curated port list
apparatus_b.scan_model: its own purpose-built scanners, banner grabbing and protocol parsing across roughly thirty application-layer protocols

documentation_ledger.$comment: Section 43. Every request made, in order. First-party only for load-bearing gate closure.

requests.sought: data update cycles and scan timestamp semantics
timestamp and observation-time semantics of response records
requests.established: two temporal fields: @timestamp is the index time, scan_date is when the scanning activity that generated the response occurred. Each document is a single service response collected during scanning, keyed by (uri, ip): a discrete point-in-time observation rather than a merged state.

observed_at marks when a service was obtained by a Censys scan and is NOT searchable, because service observation timestamps change too rapidly to publish. The searchable host-level last_updated_at reflects the time of the latest CHANGE, and a host observed daily for five days without change carries a last_updated_at from five days ago.
per-host timelines preserve a snapshot per scan and permit comparing two scan events, with access windows bounded by plan tier. This is per-host inspection, not an aggregate window selector.

requests.sought: how the queryable dataset is constructed in time terms
requests.established: the queryable dataset is a MERGED CURRENT STATE built from individual scans. host.services.scan_time marks when a service was LAST observed. No mechanism is documented for restricting an aggregate count to services observed within a specified past window. Under high density, service data represents a SAMPLING of service details.
RFC 4253 section 4.2: the server sends SSH-protoversion-softwareversion SP comments CR LF immediately on connection and before any negotiation, and other server output lines must not begin with SSH-.

requests.sought: an affirmative statement that host observations come from its own scanning
requests.established: the index page carries no such statement, and it separates primary internet scan data from auxiliary enrichment drawn from DNS registries, WHOIS and certificate sources.
